q: True or false: A two-way hospital ramp needs 2.44 m clear width.
n: 1.22 m one way, 2.44 m two ways. Remember this: "6-8 and 4-8." Corridors: 6 ft (1.83 m) for non-patient, 8 ft (2.44 m) for beds. Ramps: 4 ft (1.22 m) one-way, 8 ft (2.44 m) two-way. Slope 1:12, like 12 months to climb 1 year.

q: Fill in the blank: Ramp slope shall not be steeper than 1:___.
n: 1:12, the same ratio used in BP 344.

q: Match the width: 1.83 m (6 ft) belongs to which element?
o: Corridor not used for bed or stretcher transport
n: Think "6 ft for walking, 8 ft for wheeling beds."

q: True or false: Without a multi-level ramp, the hospital elevator must accommodate at least a patient bed.
n: Bed-size elevator is the fallback when there is no ramp.
